title: The symmetric algebra is graded by the images of the tensor powers
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-module. Let $\mathrm T_R(M)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathrm T^n_R(M)$ be the tensor algebra ($\mathrm T^0_R(M)=R$, $\mathrm T^n_R(M)=M^{\otimes_R n}$), $J\subseteq\mathrm T_R(M)$ the two-sided ideal generated by the elements $x\otimes y-y\otimes x$ ($x,y\in M$), $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)=\mathrm T_R(M)/J$ with quotient map $\pi$, and $\iota_M=\pi|_M:M\to\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. For $n\ge0$ let $\operatorname{Sym}^n_R(M)=\pi(\mathrm T^n_R(M))$, the $R$-submodule of $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ spanned by the products $\iota_M(x_1)\cdots\iota_M(x_n)$ with $x_1,\dots,x_n\in M$ (so $\operatorname{Sym}^0_R(M)=R\cdot1$ and $\operatorname{Sym}^1_R(M)=\iota_M(M)$). Then $J=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}(J\cap\mathrm T^n_R(M))$, and consequently $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\operatorname{Sym}^n_R(M)$ as $R$-modules: every element of $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ is a finite sum $\sum_n s_n$ with $s_n\in\operatorname{Sym}^n_R(M)$, and the $s_n$ are uniquely determined by it. Moreover $\operatorname{Sym}^n_R(M)\cdot\operatorname{Sym}^m_R(M)\subseteq\operatorname{Sym}^{n+m}_R(M)$ for all $n,m\ge0$.
